scenes.big: Is the sun hurting your eyes?
scenes.en: UV light harms more than your skin.
scenes.say: Chennai sun is strong all year. And its UV light can harm your eyes, not just your skin.

scenes.en: Invisible UV rays reach the eye's surface and its lens. Damage adds up over years.
scenes.ta: கண்ணுக்குத் தெரியாத UV கதிர்கள் – பாதிப்பு ஆண்டுக்கணக்கில் சேரும்
scenes.say: UV rays are invisible. They reach the surface of your eye and the lens inside it, and the damage adds up over many years.

scenes.en: Years of sun exposure raise the risk of cataract and growths on the white of the eye.
scenes.say: Did you know? Studies show years of sun exposure raise the risk of cataract, and of fleshy growths on the white of the eye.

scenes.en: Look for '100% UV protection' or 'UV400'. Darker is not always safer.
scenes.ta: UV400 அல்லது 100% UV பாதுகாப்பு உள்ள கண்ணாடி
scenes.say: Step one. Wear sunglasses marked UV four hundred, or one hundred percent UV protection. A darker lens is not always safer.

scenes.en: A cap or wide hat blocks light from above.
scenes.say: Step two. Add a cap or a wide hat, and use the shade around midday.

scenes.en: Children's eyes let in more UV. Sand and water reflect extra light.
scenes.say: Step three. Protect children too. Their eyes let in more UV, and sand and water reflect even more light.

scenes.en: Not even during an eclipse. Sudden blind spot or blur? See an eye specialist urgently.
scenes.say: Never look straight at the sun, even during an eclipse. If you notice a blind spot or sudden blur, see an eye specialist urgently.
